name: Parthenon on the Acropolis
description: The quintessential Doric marble temple of Athena, an official New 7 Wonders Top Global Finalist.
history: Built during the Golden Age of Athens under Pericles as the centerpiece of the Acropolis complex, housing the giant chryselephantine statue of Athena Parthenos.
construction: Constructed from 20,000 tons of white Pentelic marble with subtle optical entasis curves so the lines appear perfectly straight to the human eye.
architecture: Peripteral octastyle Doric temple with Ionic frieze elements, pediment sculptures, and metopes depicting battles of gods, giants, and centaurs.
significance: The enduring global symbol of Western democracy, classical philosophy, and architectural harmony. Official Top 21 Finalist in the 2007 New 7 Wonders campaign.
currentStatus: Standing and conserved on the Acropolis rock in Athens.
wonderCategory: New7Wonders Top Global Finalist & Ancient Masterpiece
wonderHistoricalContext: Celebrated for 2,500 years as the highest peak of Greek classical architecture, finishing in the premier Top 21 Global Finalists in the official 2007 New 7 Wonders worldwide ballot.
